Does delphi-17cf (6960P) really run the same FAST_CORE_RANGES as the 6962P hosts (July host comparison says yes)? If so, 6960P tron cores 75-78 and 87-94 are clamped. Needs a get-assoc read on 17cf against its own map section.

Why did the two-tier policy signature survive a boot with the unit masked (Gate C, 2026-08-01)? The masked-against-installed reboot A/B was never completed, and the 2026-07-09 step in nightly dispersion that coincided with the policy install is unexplained.
How should the boot service (or a platformd-owned apply) sequence with ci-runner.sh's 02:45 UTC inference/up and the nightly lease? Flagged for review in July, never closed.

Should the FE un-clamp be re-justified on today's engine before shipping? The only evidence is July 2026 (gpt-oss-120b tp4, +1.12 % +/- 0.21 decode at 8 users); the Sept runtron campaign cannot see it.
Does the policy run on delphi-3c51, 3bd6 and 3af6 today, and which tool binary and sudoers entries exist there? The Sept files cover only 3bda.

What is the per-host expected frequency under the policy given BIOS differences (C6 disabled on 3bda; BIOS 92011500 on 3bda against 92011600 on 3c51)? Only 3bda and 3af6 were measured (3900 against 4100 MHz on the 80-core shape in July).
Is a per-instance or per-socket policy (associations scoped to one instance's cores) wanted, given that the CLOS windows are shared per die and a half-machine change was shown to work on socket 1?

If platformd derives the fast set from the map, which roles belong in it? Evidence: tron_cores + peer_cores + siblings (shipped), plus rinzler_cores (July, +1 % in serving); dev_cores and platform_cores measured as no gain in runtron (within +/-0.5 %).
What does a platformd health check report when the frequency observable disagrees with the register readback (the June 'readback-correct, runtime-wrong' case)? No decision recorded.
Which platformd version and which host CPUs are in the production fleet (resource-map.yaml lists only granite_rapids_6960p/6962p as Intel entries); only delphi-3bda (6962P, kernel 6.8) was measured.

Does platformd want a per-engine or host-level way to set TRON_AMX_DISABLE (rollback) or TRON_HWATTN_EARLY_LAUNCH_MIN_B? Today only config.env (host-global) and platformd-written instance-N.env exist, and explicit provisioning sends only the model shape.

The 2026-09-17 observation of 501 M AMX-busy cycles (57 % of the CPU-attention arm) under FPGA attention with a warm prefix cache is unexplained; production traffic with shared prefixes may put real attention work on AMX on FPGA-attention engines.
No measurement exists of the effect of placing two AMX attention workers on SMT siblings of one physical core; tron does not check it and the 6962P tron_cores lists include HT-sibling ids.

Intel-only tp4 TPS jumps on the first AMX night (qwen tp4 +18.4 %, gpt-oss +10.8 %, llama-70b tp4 +3.6 %) are unattributed (hypothesis PR #4534); the mixtral TTFT +2.4 % Intel-only change is untested against the kill switch.

No production use case has been defined for CPU attention with AMX on ingested models; measured decode is about 20 % below FPGA attention at the nightly load, so USE_HW_ATTN should stay unset for them unless FPGA capacity is unavailable.

The AMX gain at production loads other than the measured cells (2/4/8 users per engine, prompts 1024-4096 for llama-8b; 2 users per engine 1024-8192 for qwen CPU attention) is not measured; gains at 1 user or very short prompts are near zero.

Boot-sticky policy amplification of the gpt-oss dispersion: dispersion stepped 1.5% -> 4.7% on 3bda at the 2026-07-09 reboot/policy install; the designed reboot A/B (policy masked -> installed -> masked, >=10 draws per boot) was never run.
